miles: Hey team — first-day setup question. I ran `make dev` and Postgres container starts but migrations fail with:
```
FATAL:  database files are incompatible with the server
DETAIL: The database cluster was initialized by PostgreSQL version 13, but the server is running version 14.
```
Postgres keeps restarting. I'm on an M1 Mac and I pulled the repo from a coworker who used Intel. Any safe way to reset local DB without losing the seeds I added?

irina: Welcome, miles! :wave: That error usually means the PGDATA dir was created by a different PG version or architecture (amd64 vs arm64). If you don't need the old data, delete the volume and let compose recreate it. Quick checks: `docker volume ls` and `docker ps -a` to find the container.

sam: If you want to keep a backup first, run this from any host with docker to snapshot the named volume to a tar: 
````
docker run --rm -v project_postgres_data:/data -v $PWD:/out alpine sh -c "cd /data && tar -cf /out/pgdata-backup.tar ."
````
We also have `dev/backup_local_db.sh` in the repo that wraps this.

irina: Steps I use: 1) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml down` 2) `docker volume rm project_postgres_data` (or the correct volume) 3) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres` 4) `make dev` — migrations and seeds should run. If your compose uses a host bind (e.g., `./tmp/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`) move that host folder out of the way.

devops-bot: Note: On Apple Silicon prefer arm64/ multi-arch images. See internal guide: https://redwood.dev/internal/dev-setup#arm-m1. Using amd64 emulation can hide architecture+version mismatches.

miles: Thanks — I did `docker volume ls` and saw `project_postgres_data` and `project_redis_data`. Backed up the volume to a tar, removed the old volume, restarted compose and migrations completed. All good now, appreciate the quick tips! :tada:
